question: What is the main purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: Conducting laboratory research on new medications
options.B: Treating individual patients in hospital wards
options.C: Tracking health data to guide planning and action
options.D: Managing hospital financial budgets and staff

explanation: Surveillance focuses on collecting and analyzing population health data so authorities can take proper action to protect the public. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why is disease surveillance compared to an early warning radar?

options.A: It predicts natural disasters like floods that cause water contamination
options.B: It measures the exact wind speed during an airborne disease outbreak
options.C: It helps health workers spot unusual illness clusters before they spread
options.D: It uses satellite technology to track patient movements across borders

explanation: Just like a radar warns of approaching danger, surveillance detects disease spikes early so health teams can respond quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Which surveillance type relies on healthcare workers sending routine reports without special prompting?
explanation: Passive surveillance relies on routine reporting by clinics and hospitals without outside prompting, making it simple but prone to underreporting. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: Public health officers visit local clinics and review registers directly to find hidden cases during a cholera outbreak. What type of surveillance is this?
explanation: When health staff proactively visit facilities to search for cases rather than waiting for reports, they are conducting active surveillance. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: What is the final step in the core disease surveillance cycle?
explanation: Data collection and analysis are useless unless they lead directly to meaningful public health action and control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: Why is analyzing data by time, place, and person important in surveillance?

options.A: It helps pinpoint where and among whom an outbreak is spreading
options.B: It calculates the exact financial cost of running a primary health center
options.C: It determines the educational background of infected community members
options.D: It proves which doctors wrote the most accurate medical prescriptions

explanation: Breaking down data by time, place, and person gives epidemiologists clues about the source and spread of a disease. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the main operational strategy used for disease surveillance in Nigerian health facilities?
explanation: The IDSR strategy is the standardized framework used across Nigerian health facilities to detect and report priority diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why are community informants and patent medicine vendors important for surveillance in Nigeria?

options.A: They help capture health events in rural areas far from formal clinics
options.B: They possess advanced laboratory equipment for testing blood samples
options.C: They write the official national epidemiological weekly bulletins
options.D: They are responsible for funding all primary health care centers

explanation: Many rural citizens visit local medicine vendors or traditional attendants first, making these community actors vital for early case detection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: What is the purpose of drawing an epidemic curve during an investigation?

options.A: To measure the physical distance between infected houses
options.B: To test the purity of local water supplies in a lab
options.C: To visualize how the infection spread over time
options.D: To calculate the total budget spent on patient drugs

explanation: An epidemic curve is a graph that shows the onset of cases over time, helping investigators understand the outbreak's pattern. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: An investigation team sets a strict standard for what symptoms and lab results a patient must have to be counted in an outbreak. What is this standard called?
explanation: A case definition sets clear criteria (clinical signs, time, place) so all investigators count the exact same type of cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: Which of the following is a direct surveillance responsibility for a clinical nurse?

options.A: Enforcing federal health policies in the national parliament
options.B: Importing international vaccines for national distribution
options.C: Conducting post-mortem examinations on all deceased patients
options.D: Reporting suspected cases of priority diseases immediately

explanation: Nurses must promptly notify public health authorities when they encounter suspected cases of dangerous or reportable diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why are community health nurses considered the frontline eyes and ears of health surveillance?

options.A: They have direct, daily contact with patients and local communities
options.B: They manage the federal budget for disease control programs
options.C: They spend most of their working hours analyzing computer software
options.D: They have exclusive authority to declare national health emergencies

explanation: Nurses see patients first at clinic visits and outreach posts, placing them in the best position to spot unusual disease patterns early. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: What is NOT a typical challenge faced by disease surveillance systems in developing settings?

options.A: Delays in transporting clinical samples due to poor roads
options.B: An overabundance of fully staffed reference laboratories
options.C: Inadequate funding for rapid response outbreak teams
options.D: Poor reporting compliance by overburdened health workers

explanation: A lack of laboratories and equipment is a major challenge, not an overabundance of them. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: How does the 'One Health' approach improve disease surveillance systems?

options.A: It connects human, animal, and environmental health sectors to catch zoonotic threats
options.B: It restricts disease reporting to only one central government agency
options.C: It combines all nursing duties into a single administrative job description
options.D: It ensures that every hospital uses only one single brand of medical computer

explanation: Many outbreaks start in animals or the environment, so One Health brings these sectors together for better early detection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)
